findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). The class is therefore abstract, and `Detector.detector_handler` (which does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class` for any `Detector` whose `type` is `metric_alert_fire`. `MetricAlertFire` still registers this class as its `detector_handler`, so `process_detectors` will crash on such detectors instead of logging/skipping. Either implement the abstract methods (even with stub bodies) or remove `detector_handler` from `MetricAlertFire` until a real implementation exists.

findings.title: Expected occurrence in test_dedupe is built with the wrong group key
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` the expected occurrence is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)`, but the handler is invoked with group key `"group_key"`. The real call to `build_occurrence_and_event_data` will produce a fingerprint of `["<detector_id>:group_key"]` while the expected `IssueOccurrence` has `["<detector_id>:val1"]`. Since `IssueOccurrence` is a dataclass with field equality, the `== expected_result` assertion compares different fingerprints; the test either fails or, if it currently passes, indicates the comparison is not actually checking the occurrence. The expected occurrence should be built with `"group_key"`.

findings.title: Mock occurrence builder ignores `value`, so tests cannot detect wrong values passed to the hook
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value` but never uses it in the produced `IssueOccurrence` or event data. Several tests (e.g. `test_results_on_change` evaluating with value 100, `test_dedupe` with 8, `test_state_results_multi_group` with 10 for `group_2`) build the expected occurrence with a hard-coded `6`, and they pass only because `value` is discarded. This means a regression that passes the wrong `value` into `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (the new hook this PR adds) would go unnoticed. Include `value` in the mock output (e.g. in `evidence_data`) and pass the actual evaluated value in the expectations.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still states 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`'. Implementers reading the docstring will be misled about the contract; update it to describe the dict keyed by group key.
